# Popover

Figma: [05i. Popover](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=3925-2734) · Family: 05 Feedback · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-01-01

A click/tap-triggered floating panel anchored to a trigger, holding richer content than a Tooltip - a title, body, and actions you can interact with. Non-blocking (dismiss on outside-click or Esc). Built on the Tooltip bubble+arrow pattern. Placement × Direction, RTL/LTR.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/popover/reference.png`

### Popover

Click or tap anchored floating panel with title, close, body and an action or link, built on the Tooltip bubble and arrow. Non-blocking: dismiss on outside tap or Esc.

Level: molecule · Contains: Button, IconButton

Use when:
- Explaining Qualified investor with a Learn more link next to a tier label
- Quick filter or small form anchored to a toolbar button on web or back-office
- Confirm-in-place for a minor action
- Contextual help that needs a link

Don't use when:
- Passive hover hint with text only: use Tooltip
- A list of actions: use Menu
- A required decision: use Dialog or Modal
- On phones or heavy content: use BottomSheet

Accessibility: Trigger has aria-expanded and aria-controls; move focus into the panel on open and back on close; Esc closes.

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Popover sits between Tooltip and Modal: more than a hint, less than a blocking dialog. Use it for contextual explanations with a link, small forms, filters, quick actions, or confirm-in-place - anything anchored to what the user just clicked.

### Anatomy

A shadowed bubble with a directional arrow pointing at the trigger, and a free-form content slot.

- Bubble - surface (bg/elevated), border, Radius/8, drop shadow.
- Arrow - points at the anchor; its side is set by Placement.
- Content slot - title + close, body, and an action row (link or buttons). Fully overridable.

### Placement

top · right · bottom · left - where the popover sits relative to the trigger (the arrow points back at it). It should flip to stay on-screen.

### Direction - LTR and RTL

RTL is primary - text aligns right, the close button and content mirror.

### When to use

- Tooltip (04d) - a passive, hover text hint. No interaction. Use for short labels.
- Popover - click-triggered, interactive, free-form content. Use for explanations-with-a-link, small forms, filters, confirm-in-place.
- Menu - a popover specialised for a list of actions/options.
- Modal - blocks the screen for a required decision. Popover is non-blocking; dismiss on outside-click.
- On mobile - a popover usually resolves to a Bottom Sheet or Action Sheet (Lazyweb research across DoorDash, iOS share/action sheets, NYT): bottom-anchored, a prominent CTA Button + an X IconButton. For heavy content on small screens, prefer BottomSheet over an anchored popover.

### Code examples

```typescript
<Popover placement="top" dir="rtl">
  <Popover.Trigger><IconButton icon="info" /></Popover.Trigger>
  <Popover.Content title="مستثمر مؤهل" onClose={close}>
    يفتح هذا المستوى صفقات مخصصة للمؤهلين…
    <Link href="/tiers">إعرف أكثر</Link>
  </Popover.Content>
</Popover>
```

### Usage - Do and Don't

Do

Anchor it to the trigger and point the arrow back at it - keep content short with one clear action.

Don’t

Don’t cram a full form or long content into a popover - if it needs the screen, use a Modal or a page.

### Notes from the maintainer

> **Info:** Popover reuses the Tooltip’s bubble + arrow pattern (bg/elevated, Radius/8, shadow) - so hints and popovers feel like one family. Only the content differs: text-only vs interactive slot.

> **Tip:** The content slot here (title · close · body · link) is a representative default - override it with forms, filters, or action rows as needed.

> **Warning:** Popover is non-blocking. For anything that needs a decision before continuing, use a Modal - don’t force a popover to behave like one.

> **Tip:** Mobile: research shows “popovers” on phones are typically bottom sheets / action sheets with one prominent CTA + an X close - not tiny floating bubbles. The action here is our Button (text/primary) and close is our IconButton, so both scale to a tap-friendly bottom-sheet footer when needed.
